name: Webflow
oneLiner: Visual website builder with a built-in CMS and hosting, billed as a Site plan for each published site plus a Workspace where extra editors are paid seats.
summary: Webflow is a visual site builder that gives designers control over layout and code and hosts the result, with a CMS for blogs and other structured content. Each site published to a custom domain needs its own Site plan (Premium is the CMS plan), and everyone besides the Workspace owner needs a paid seat, so the bill grows with both editors and traffic. Since May 2026 Premium includes 50 GB of bandwidth a month, and more is sold in tiers up to 2.5 TB.
notFor: Sites with heavy traffic that want a flat price, since bandwidth past 50 GB a month is billed in tiers
Stores that need a full ecommerce back office (Standard is capped at 500 items and adds a 2% fee)
Owners who want a simple template editor with no design learning curve
pros: Premium includes 20,000 CMS items and 40 Collections for $39/mo month-to-month or $25/mo billed yearly
Content editors can be added as $19/mo Limited seats without upgrading the free Starter Workspace
Custom code on Basic and Premium, code components on Premium, and HTML/CSS export on paid Workspace plans
On Basic and Premium the first month over the bandwidth limit is not charged, and Webflow notifies you before any upgrade
New Site and Workspace plan purchases are refundable within 14 days, monthly or annual
The free Starter plan has no time limit for building and testing on a webflow.io subdomain
cons: Bandwidth is metered: Premium includes 50 GB a month, and at 1 TB it costs $599/mo month-to-month
Bot traffic counts toward bandwidth, and two months in a row over the limit triggers a non-refundable automatic upgrade
Site plans and Workspace seats are separate bills, so the real cost is harder to predict than a single plan price
Seats, add-ons and renewals are non-refundable, and cancelling still leaves you paying the rest of the term
Ecommerce Standard adds a 2% transaction fee on top of Stripe or PayPal fees
Leaving is work: code export needs a paid Workspace plan, CMS content exports one Collection at a time, and forms stop working
